{
"Asynchronous Programming": "A programming paradigm that enables tasks to execute independently of the main program flow, allowing operations to proceed without blocking execution while waiting for other operations to complete.",
"Async/Await Syntax": "A language-level construct, notably in Python, that provides a readable syntax for defining and invoking asynchronous coroutines using the 'async' and 'await' keywords.",
"Coroutine": "A specialized function that can suspend and resume its execution, yielding control back to the event loop when awaiting another operation.",
"Event Loop": "A core construct in asynchronous programming that continuously manages, schedules, and dispatches the execution of tasks, coroutines, and futures on a single thread.",
"Task": "A unit of work that wraps a coroutine and is scheduled for execution by the event loop, representing an ongoing asynchronous operation.",
"Future": "An object representing a value or result that is not yet available but is expected to be produced by an asynchronous operation at some point in the future.",
"Callback": "A function registered to be invoked automatically when a specific event occurs, such as when a task or future completes its execution.",
"asyncio.gather": "A Python asyncio function that concurrently runs multiple awaitable objects, aggregating their results and allowing them to be managed as a single operation.",
"Execution Blocking": "A condition where a program's execution is halted while waiting for an operation to complete, preventing other tasks from making progress.",
"Python": "A high-level, general-purpose programming language that provides native support for asynchronous programming through its asyncio library and async/await syntax.",
"Task Readiness Polling": "The process by which the event loop repeatedly checks tasks to determine if they are ready to resume execution or have completed their awaited operations.",
"Task Completion Handler": "A callback or routine invoked by the event loop when a task finishes execution, used to process results or handle any exceptions raised."
}
